chunks.heading: Eligible entities
chunks.text: To claim R&D tax offsets, entities must be "R&D entities" and incur notional deductions of at least $20,000 on eligible R&D activities. An R&D entity is a corporation incorporated under Australian law, foreign law (if Australian tax resident), or foreign law with a relevant double tax agreement and permanent establishment in Australia. The following are explicitly ineligible: an individual, a corporate limited partnership, or an exempt entity (where your entire income is exempt from income tax).
chunks.sourceTitle: Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive

chunks.heading: Core R&D activities
chunks.text: Core R&D activities are experimental activities where the outcome can't be known or determined in advance on the basis of current knowledge, information or experience; they involve a systematic progression of work that is based on principles of established science, proceeding from hypothesis to experiment, observation and evaluation; and they aim at generating new knowledge (including about creating new knowledge or improved materials, products, devices, processes or services).
chunks.sourceTitle: Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive

chunks.heading: Supporting R&D activities
chunks.text: Supporting activities are directly related to core R&D activities, or undertaken for the dominant purpose of supporting core R&D activities. The dominant purpose requirement applies to activities that produce goods/services or are excluded from core R&D classification.
chunks.sourceTitle: Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive

chunks.heading: Notional deduction threshold
chunks.text: Entities must incur at least $20,000 in notional deductions annually to claim offsets, with limited exceptions for Research Service Provider contracted expenditure and Cooperative Research Centre contributions below this threshold.
chunks.sourceTitle: Eligibility for the R&D tax incentive

chunks.heading: Salary expenditure
chunks.text: Organisations may claim costs for salaries, wages, allowances, bonuses, overtime and penalty rate payments, along with leave entitlements and superannuation contributions, for employees directly conducting R&D activities. Support staff salaries — such as administrative or general management personnel — cannot be claimed unless directly linked to R&D work.

chunks.heading: Contracted services (Research Service Providers)
chunks.text: Expenditure paid to Research Service Providers (RSPs) registered with the Department of Industry, Science and Resources bypasses the standard $20,000 threshold. Contracting with other parties requires meeting this minimum threshold. Contract documentation should show the nature of the work and its relation to your R&D activities.

chunks.heading: Depreciating assets
chunks.text: The decline in value of tangible assets used for R&D qualifies, calculated through modified Division 40 rules. Assets cannot be pooled after claiming R&D deductions.

chunks.heading: Administrative costs
chunks.text: Organisations may claim rent or lease payments, light and power, property rates and taxes, cleaning, and certain insurance costs directly linked to R&D operations.

chunks.heading: Record-keeping requirements
chunks.text: Documentation must support claimed amounts. For mixed-use employees, organisations should maintain time sheets or job cards demonstrating R&D allocation. Contract expenditure requires records showing how work under the contract relates to your activities, potentially including meeting minutes and progress reports.

chunks.heading: Excluded expenditure
chunks.text: Non-deductible items include tax agent fees for preparing a registration application or tax return claims, and salary costs lacking proper PAYG withholding.
